**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/30 (Tue) 13:35
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] `update-rc.d` is a command-line tool used to manage system startup scripts on Debian and Ubuntu Linux distributions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] `update-rc.d` is used to create, remove, and manage symbolic links in the /etc/rc[runlevel].d/ directories that point to service scripts in the /etc/init.d/ directory.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The basic syntax for the `update-rc.d` command is: `update-rc.d [-n] [-f] [--remove] scriptname defaults|remove|{start|stop} N`.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The command `sudo update-rc.d supervisor defaults` creates symbolic links for the supervisor script to start automatically at boot.
- [USER] Asks about runlevels in /etc/rc[runlevel].d.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Runlevels correspond to the state of the system and which services are running, with standard runlevels being 0 (Halt), 1 (Single-user mode), 2 (Multi-user mode without networking), 3 (Multi-user mode with networking), 4 (Not used/User-definable), 5 (Multi-user mode with GUI), and 6 (Reboot).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The /etc/rc[runlevel].d/ directories contain symbolic links to scripts in /etc/init.d/ that control services during startup and shutdown.
- [USER] Asks if Supervisor should be reloaded after changing a script.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Yes, Supervisor needs to be reloaded for changes to take effect, using `sudo supervisorctl reload` or `sudo service supervisor restart`.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Reloading Supervisor will not restart the services themselves; it will just reload the new configuration.
- [USER] Asks how to stop a script.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] To stop a script managed by Supervisor, use `sudo supervisorctl stop script_name`.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] You can check the status of the script with `sudo supervisorctl status script_name` and stop all scripts with `sudo supervisorctl stop all`.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] To completely remove a script from Supervisor's configuration, use `sudo supervisorctl remove script_name`.
- [USER] Reports an error "cannot open display" when using Gedit editor.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The error occurs when trying to run gedit on a remote server over SSH without the correct DISPLAY variable set.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] To fix this, use `ssh -X user@your
